newsitem.title: CHINA: China capital festive for HK handover despite rain.
newsitem.headline: China capital festive for HK handover despite rain.

text.p: A festive mood permeated China on Monday with revellers flocking to Beijing's Tiananmen Square to celebrate the Hong Kong handover and the Communist Party trumpeting its success in winning back the British colony.
The ruling Communist Party blew its own horn on the eve of its 76th birthday, crowing that the peaceful return of Hong Kong to Chinese sovereignty had been possible only under the communists.

"The return of Hong Kong to the motherland... has been a dream for more than 100 years but became reality step by step only under the leadership of the Communist Party," the official People's Daily said in a front-page editorial to celebrate the handover at midnight.

Late paramount leader and communist veteran Deng Xiaoping negotiated the return of capitalist Hong Kong, reaching agreement with London in 1984 to recover the territory, seized after Britain defeated a weak imperial China in the 19th-century Opium Wars.

The editorial was the latest installment in a propaganda campaign that has billed the handover as one of the most important events of the year, if not the decade, and as a moment that will wash away a century and a half of national disgrace.

Tens of thousands of revellers defied rain to flock to the square just hours before the midnight return of Hong Kong to Chinese rule, and organisers of the official celebrations said they were undeterred by the damp.
"If it rains tonight, everything will proceed as normal," said a stern-faced member of the paramilitary People's Armed Police patrolling the square.

Carrying umbrellas or simply ignoring a misty drizzle after a thunderstorm drenched the capital, Chinese packed the square for one last glimpse of the huge decorations before the vast area is sealed off at 3.00 p.m. (0700 GMT) to the general public for the official ceremony.
"This is a last chance to come to Tiananmen and then we will watch the celebrations on television," one retired worker said as she clutched small souvenir Chinese and Hong Kong flags.
"I just hope Heaven doesn't cry on our celebrations," one Beijing college student said, gesturing at the clouds hanging over the square.

"A few months ago, there were millions of seconds left until the Hong Kong return, but now there's just a little more than 40,000," the college student said, posing in front of the giant clock counting down the days and seconds to the handover.

China's communists moved to allay concerns over the stationing of People's Liberation Army (PLA) soldiers in the territory, telling the garrison as it prepared to depart that they must love Hong Kong people and protect their prosperity.

"With your actual deeds (you must) win the support and love of the Hong Kong people," General Liu Huaqing, vice-chairman of the Central Military Commission, told a departure ceremony for the troops in southern Shenzhen on the border with Hong Kong.

The People's Liberation Army garrison for Hong Kong is due to enter the territory in two waves, with 509 marching in at 9.00 p.m. (1300 GMT) on Monday and another 4,000 sweeping in by land, sea and air just six hours after the handover.
Many people in Hong Kong view the arrival of the PLA with alarm, recalling the army's June, 1989, crushing of student-led demonstrations in Tiananmen Square. Hundreds were killed.
